questions.q: Displacement of a wave is expressed as $x(t)=5 \cos \left(628 t+\frac{\pi}{2}\right) m$. The wavelength of the wave when its velocity is $300 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{x}(\mathrm{t})=5 \cos \left[628 \mathrm{t}+\frac{\pi}{2}\right] \mathrm{m} \\ & \text { velocity }\left(\mathrm{v}_\omega\right)=300 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{w}}=\frac{\omega}{\mathrm{K}} \\ & 300=\frac{628}{\mathrm{~K}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{~K}=\frac{628}{300} \\ & \frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}=\frac{628}{300} \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{2 \times 3.14 \times 300}{628} \\ & \lambda=2 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
The equations of two waves are given by :

y1=5sin2πx-vt cm

y2=3sin2πx-vt+1.5 cm

These waves are simultaneously passing through a string. The amplitude of the resulting wave is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given equations can be written as,

y1=5sin2πx-2πvt cm and

y2=3sin2πx-2πvt+3π cm

From the given equations we can conclude that the phase difference between the waves is 3π i.e. odd multiple of π. Therefore, destructive interference will happen.

A=A1-A2=2 cm

questions.q: The ratio of speed of sound in hydrogen gas to the speed of sound in oxygen gas at the same temperature is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the speed of sound in hydrogen gas is given by

vH2=γRTMH2   ...1

The formula to calculate the speed of sound in oxygen is given by

vO2=γRTMO2   ...2

Divide equation (1) by (2) and simplify to obtain the required ratio.

vH2vO2=MO2MH2   ...3

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required ratio.

vH2vO2=322= 4:1

questions.q: Two light beams of intensities <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mi>I</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mi>I</mi></math> interfere on a screen. The phase difference between these beams on the screen at point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is zero and at point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>π</mi></math>. The difference of resultant intensities, at the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math>, will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The resultant intensity is given by Inet =I1+I2+2I1I2cosϕ

Now, for Imax, phase angle is ϕ=0 and for Imin, phase angle is ϕ=π.

Thus, Imax=I1+I22=9I+4I2=25I

And Imin=I1-I22=9I-4I2=I

The difference of resultant intensities is Imax-Imin=25I-I=24I

questions.q: A sonometer wire of resonating length $90 \mathrm{~cm}$ has a fundamental frequency of $400 \mathrm{~Hz}$ when kept under some tension. The resonating length of the wire with fundamental frequency of $600 \mathrm{~Hz}$ under same tension _____$\mathrm{cm}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{f}_0=400 \mathrm{~Hz} ; \mathrm{v}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{T}}{\mu}}=\text { constant } \\ & \frac{\lambda}{2}=\mathrm{L} ; \quad \mathrm{v}=\mathrm{f}_0 \lambda\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{v}}{2 \mathrm{f}_0}=\mathrm{L} \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}=2 \mathrm{Lf}_0 \\ & \mathrm{~L}^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{2 \mathrm{f}^{\prime}}=\frac{2 \mathrm{Lf}_0}{2 \mathrm{f}^{\prime}} \\ & =\frac{\mathrm{Lf}_0}{\mathrm{f}^{\prime}}=\frac{90 \times 400}{600}=60\end{aligned}$
